transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thank you. Well, what finally made me come in today is this physical tension I can't seem to shake. My neck, my shoulders, and my jaw are just tight almost all the time now. It’s... it's like I'm constantly bracing for bad news, even when I'm just sitting at my desk at school or trying to watch TV at night. It just won't let up.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried most days, even when there’s no clear reason for it?

Yeah, I do. It's pretty much every day. My mind just keeps jumping from one thing to another. I'll be worrying about whether the contractors missed something at the house, and then I'm stressing over whether my lesson plans are slipping at school. Or I'll start worrying that the kids in the robotics club are falling behind... and then I just feel like I'm disappointing my wife and family by not keeping everything under control. It's just a constant cycle.
Have you noticed these physical symptoms, like the tension in your neck, shoulders, and jaw, even when you're not actively stressed or anxious?

I'm not really sure. It's... well, it's hard to tell, because I feel like I'm almost always actively stressed about something. I don't really have moments where my mind is completely quiet to even check if the tension is still there without the worry. It just feels like the tightness is a constant background thing now. I couldn't really tell you if it happens when I'm completely relaxed, because I just don't feel completely relaxed lately.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about your physical symptoms, like being afraid that the tension in your neck or shoulders means something serious is wrong with your body?

No, not really. I mean... I know it's just because I'm so wound up all the time. It's uncomfortable, and it's really frustrating to deal with, but I don't sit around thinking it's a disease or some major medical problem. I'm pretty sure it's just all the stress carrying over into my muscles, so I don't really worry about it being something serious with my body.
Do you feel like you have a hard time controlling your worries, even when you try to stop thinking about things?

Yeah, I really do. I mean, I can tell myself to just stop and focus on the class right in front of me, but... it doesn't really work. Just one small thought—like a late invoice for the house, or noticing a student falling behind—it sets off this whole chain of what-ifs. And once that starts, I just can't seem to shut it down, no matter how hard I try.
Do you often feel restless, on edge, or unable to relax, even when there’s no specific reason to be worried?

Yeah, definitely. I just feel wound up most of the day, to be honest. It's like... well, like I'm always waiting for something else to go wrong. Even when there isn't a direct problem right in front of me, I can't sit still. I'll catch myself pacing around the classroom a lot, or... constantly checking my phone between periods to see if there are messages from the contractor. I just can't seem to settle down and relax.
Do you often feel fatigued or low on energy, even when you haven't been doing anything physically or mentally demanding?

Yeah, I do. Honestly, by the time the last bell rings, I just feel completely wrung out. And it's... it's in a way that a decent night's sleep or a quiet Sunday doesn't really fix. Even if the day wasn't that demanding, just sitting down to grade a short stack of quizzes feels like pushing through mud. I just have no energy left.
Do you often have trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking up feeling unrested, even when you're tired?

No, not really. I mean, I'm exhausted, like I said, so once I actually get into bed, I usually fall right asleep. I don't really wake up in the middle of the night either. It's just the daytime when I'm so drained, but the sleep itself seems okay.
Have you found yourself spending a lot of time thinking about your physical symptoms, like your tight neck or shoulders, and worrying about what they might mean?

No, not really. I mean, my neck and shoulders get stiff, sure, but I don't really worry about what it means. I just figure it's from the stress, or... you know, hunching over my desk grading papers all day. I don't spend time thinking it's a sign of some larger medical issue or anything like that.
Have you been worrying excessively about a number of everyday things for most days over the past six months or more?

Yeah, I have. It feels like my mind just keeps jumping from one thing to another. I'll be worrying about whether the contractors missed something at the house, and then right away I'm stressing over whether my lesson plans are slipping, or if the kids in my robotics club are falling behind. And... I don't know, it just turns into this constant worry that I'm disappointing my wife and family because I can't seem to keep everything under control. It's been like that most days, yeah.
